To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the mitochondrial RNA polymerse is essential for Plasmodium parasite survival even when the mitochondria are not needed for electron transport; 2) we were unable to generate a knockout parasite line by disrupting the mitochondrial RNA polymeras gene; 3) we successfully integrated a triple HA tag into the 3'end of mtRNAP gene, which is the first time a tag has been inserted at the C-terminus of this protein in any organism.
we could not generate a ρ( 0 ) parasite line in P. falciparium by disrupting the mitochondrial RNA polymerases gene, suggesting that the gene is essential in mtETC-deficient parasites.
we have failed to generate a P. falcifarum ρ(0).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a P. falciparuin parasite line lacking mtRNA, and the identification of its essential genes.
the development of a new antimalarial drug target, the mitochondrial RNA polymerases of Plasmodial parasites.
developing a method to generate a parasite line lacking mtDNAs, and our results indicate that this approach may not be feasible.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mitochondrial genome of Plasmodial parasites is not dispensable for the parasite's survival.
mtRNAP gene disruption in P. falcipurum is not possible.
the mtRNAp is essential for the survival of P. falciparium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that mtRNAP gene disruption is not possible by the current methods of double crossover recombination in P. falciprum.
the mtETC is not essential for parasite growth and survival, but that the mitochondrial genome and its RNA polymerase are essential.
we have not been able to disrupt the mtRNA polymerase in the yDHODH expressing parasites, and we are not able to generate the ρ(0), which is the ultimate goal of our work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mtRNPA is essential in Plasmodium parasites even in the absence of the mtDNA-encoded proteins.
mtRNAP might not be the only enzyme involved in mtDNA replication and that there is a redundancy in the pathways involved in mtDNA maintenance.
the mtRNAPII is essential in P. falcipurum even in the absence of the mtETCs.
